newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends up in late shortcovering rally.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends up in late shortcovering rally.

text.p: COMEX copper ended higher after a late shortcovering rally, but not enough to change the ultimately bearish mood of most brokers.
Commission house brokers appeared to gun for stops beneath support at Tuesday's September low of 104.60 cents a lb, but when it failed the market bounced higher.
The active September contract ended at 107.10 cents a lb, up 1.00 cent, while the spot month closed at 107.50 cents, 1.10 cents higher.

"There was a complete lack of interest today," said one broker. "The trade had essentially amassed some short positions and they got caught. In a market this thin, it isn't hard to pop the market up. So they covered like crazy."

Asked if the higher settlement changed the complexion of the market, he said, "Not really. Technically it looks a little better. But there was nothing behind it. I still have to think we're heading lower."
Fundamentally, the market is unchanged. LME warehouse stocks rose another 2,925 tonnes to 240,675 tonnes, the highest level since Sept 26, 1996.
The LME cash-to-three-month backwardation narrowed to $24/$28, the narrowest level since late October 1996.
"It's the middle of the summer. There's plenty of copper around. I'd expect a test of $1 a pound," said one physical trader.

In other news, Falconbridge and its strike union at its Sudbury complex are considering reopening negotiations. The mine has been on strike since last Friday and would have returned from a month-long maintanence shutdown Tuesday.
